title: WhatsApp connect
description:
Goal
- Prompt the user to connect WhatsApp at the end of their first completed evening flow.
- This prompt must never interrupt the evening flow itself; it should only appear once the flow is complete.
- The experience should mirror the existing Google account prompt pattern in spirit (clear optional CTA, dismissible, lightweight), but use the WhatsApp-specific copy and a 2-step modal flow.

Why this story exists
- Today, WhatsApp connect is effectively hidden in Settings and most users will never discover it.
- We already have a precedent for proactive account connection prompts with Google.
- We want to surface WhatsApp in-context at the best moment: immediately after the user finishes their first evening flow.

Verified implementation context in this repo
- The evening flow completion is already detectable in `src/app/chat/ChatView.tsx`.
  - The app already derives `isFlowComplete` from the latest assistant message.
  - It already detects completed evening check-ins and shows the "Advance to morning check-in" CTA.
  - This is the most natural place to trigger a post-flow WhatsApp prompt without interrupting the conversation itself.
- Existing proactive connection pattern:
  - `src/components/GoogleSignInPrompt.tsx`
  - `src/components/GoogleAuthBanner.tsx`
  - This provides a useful UX/reference pattern for optional connection prompts.
- Existing Settings/account-linking context:
  - `src/app/settings/SettingsView.tsx`
  - There is already a commented-out "Link WhatsApp" section there, which strongly suggests the intended settings entry point/path should continue to exist alongside this new prompt.
- Backend-generated user model currently includes `phoneNumber`, `telegramId`, and `googleId` on `UserModel`, but no WhatsApp prompt-tracking state.
  - Story requirement explicitly allows frontend-side generated model edits to document required backend model and endpoint changes.

Required product behavior
1. Trigger timing
- Show the WhatsApp connect popup only after the user completes their first evening flow.
- Do not show it during the flow.
- Do not block the existing end-of-flow actions or progression.
- Prefer showing it after the flow is complete and stable on screen (e.g. after completion state / next-step CTA is available).

2. Eligibility
- Show only for users who have not yet connected WhatsApp.
- Show only if the user has not already dismissed/skipped this post-evening prompt.
- Show only once for the first completed evening flow unless product explicitly decides to re-prompt later.

3. Prompt UX: first modal
Body copy:
"If it helps on busy days, you can also hear from me on WhatsApp.

It’s just for short check-ins or quick voice notes.

Anything deeper always stays in the app.

Totally optional."

Actions:
- Primary: "Connect via WhatsApp (optional)"
- Secondary: "Skip"

Behavior:
- Skip closes the prompt and permanently marks the first-evening WhatsApp prompt as dismissed/shown so it does not reappear.
- Connect proceeds to the second modal.

4. Prompt UX: second modal
Title:
- "WhatsApp basics"

Body copy:
"I’ll only use WhatsApp for:

brief check-ins

short replies

voice notes saved as journals

For anything deeper, I’ll link you back to the app."

Actions:
- Primary: "Enable WhatsApp"
- Secondary: "Cancel"

Behavior:
- Cancel returns to closed state and counts as dismissed for this first-evening prompt unless product wants re-open-on-next-visit (default assumption: dismiss permanently).
- Enable WhatsApp should start the same WhatsApp linking flow used in Settings.

5. Settings behavior
- Keep/restore a WhatsApp connection entry point in Settings so users can still connect later manually.
- Settings state should reflect whether WhatsApp is already connected.

State tracking needed
Add backend/user-profile state to support one-time prompting and connection status. Suggested fields (backend to implement; frontend can update generated models now as a contract stub):
- `whatsAppConnected?: boolean`
- `whatsAppPromptedAt?: string | null` OR `whatsAppConnectPromptShownAt?: string | null`
- Optional stronger variant if product wants clearer semantics:
  - `whatsAppConnectPromptStatus?: 'never_shown' | 'shown' | 'dismissed' | 'connected'`

Preferred minimum contract
- A boolean connection state plus a timestamp for whether the first-evening prompt has already been shown is likely enough.
- Example minimum:
  - `whatsAppConnected?: boolean`
  - `whatsAppConnectPromptShownAt?: string | null`

Backend/API work expected
- Extend the user/profile payload returned by the current "me" endpoint so the frontend can decide whether to show the prompt.
- Add/update an endpoint to mark the WhatsApp prompt as shown/dismissed when the user skips or cancels.
- Add/update an endpoint to initiate WhatsApp linking/connection from both Settings and the post-evening modal.
- If connection is phone-number-based, the backend should define whether the existing phone-link flow is reused or whether WhatsApp has a distinct connect endpoint/state.

Open product/implementation questions to resolve during implementation
- Does WhatsApp connection equal linking a WhatsApp-capable phone number, or is there a dedicated WhatsApp consent/connect flow?
- Should "Cancel" in the second modal behave the same as "Skip" and suppress future prompts? Current assumption: yes.
- Should the prompt appear immediately when evening flow completes, or after the user returns to chat idle state / after streaming is fully done? Preferred: after completion is fully rendered and no response is still streaming.
- If the user connects WhatsApp from Settings before their first evening flow, the popup should never show.

Acceptance criteria
- A user who completes their first evening flow and has not connected WhatsApp sees the optional WhatsApp prompt after completion, never during the flow.
- A user who skips/cancels the prompt does not see it again.
- A user who already connected WhatsApp does not see the prompt.
- Clicking "Connect via WhatsApp (optional)" opens the second modal.
- Clicking "Enable WhatsApp" starts the WhatsApp connection flow.
- The existing evening flow completion / advance behavior continues to work.
- A WhatsApp connection option remains available in Settings.

Implementation notes for this codebase
- Likely UI insertion point: `src/app/chat/ChatView.tsx`, alongside existing end-of-flow logic (`isFlowComplete`, evening-checkin detection, `showAdvanceButton`).
- Reusable UX references:
  - `src/components/GoogleSignInPrompt.tsx`
  - existing modal patterns under `src/app/settings/components/`
- Required account/settings touchpoint:
  - `src/app/settings/SettingsView.tsx`
- Required generated contract updates:
  - user/profile model(s) under `src/generated/backend/models/`.

features.title: Define WhatsApp user/profile contract and backend requirements
features.description:
Document and add the frontend contract stubs needed for backend implementation.

Scope
- Identify the correct generated user/profile model(s) used by the app for current-user state.
- Add WhatsApp-related fields needed for prompt eligibility and connection status.
- Prefer a minimum contract such as:
  - `whatsAppConnected?: boolean`
  - `whatsAppConnectPromptShownAt?: string | null`
- If implementation reveals a better existing home for these fields, keep semantics the same.

Backend expectations to document
- `me` payload must include WhatsApp connection state and prompt-tracking state.
- Provide endpoint(s) to:
  - initiate WhatsApp connect
  - mark the first-evening WhatsApp prompt as shown/dismissed

Acceptance criteria
- Frontend has explicit typed fields for WhatsApp connection + prompt eligibility.
- Story/code comments make the backend dependency clear enough to implement server-side.

features.title: Trigger one-time WhatsApp prompt after first completed evening flow
features.description:
Show a one-time WhatsApp prompt only after the user completes their first evening flow.

Scope
- Use the existing end-of-evening-flow detection in `src/app/chat/ChatView.tsx`.
- Do not interrupt the evening flow itself.
- Only show when all of the following are true:
  - evening flow is complete
  - user has not connected WhatsApp
  - user has not already had/dismissed this prompt
- Ensure the prompt does not repeatedly re-open on rerenders or polling updates.
- Ensure it coexists safely with the existing "Advance to morning check-in" behavior.

Acceptance criteria
- Eligible users see the prompt once after first evening flow completion.
- Ineligible users never see it.
- Prompt timing is post-flow, not mid-flow.
- Existing completion UI remains functional.

features.title: Build 2-step WhatsApp connect modal flow
features.description:
Implement the WhatsApp prompt UI as a two-step modal flow.

Step 1 copy
- "If it helps on busy days, you can also hear from me on WhatsApp.

It’s just for short check-ins or quick voice notes.

Anything deeper always stays in the app.

Totally optional."
- Actions:
  - "Connect via WhatsApp (optional)"
  - "Skip"

Step 2 copy
- Title: "WhatsApp basics"
- Body:
  - "I’ll only use WhatsApp for:

brief check-ins

short replies

voice notes saved as journals

For anything deeper, I’ll link you back to the app."
- Actions:
  - "Enable WhatsApp"
  - "Cancel"

Behavior
- Skip closes and suppresses future first-evening prompting.
- Connect opens step 2.
- Cancel closes and suppresses future first-evening prompting (unless product changes this decision later).
- Enable WhatsApp launches the connection flow.

Acceptance criteria
- Both steps match the approved copy and CTA labels.
- The component is accessible and dismiss behavior is deterministic.
- State transitions are stable across rerenders.

features.title: Integrate WhatsApp connection flow with Settings entry point
features.description:
Ensure WhatsApp can be connected both from the post-evening modal and from Settings.

Scope
- Restore or add a visible WhatsApp entry point in `src/app/settings/SettingsView.tsx`.
- Reuse the same connection initiation behavior from both places.
- Reflect connected vs unconnected state in Settings.
- If the app reuses existing phone-linking UI for WhatsApp, make that explicit and consistent.

Acceptance criteria
- Users can still manually connect WhatsApp from Settings.
- Users who already connected in Settings do not see the post-evening prompt.
- The modal and Settings use the same source of truth for connection state.

features.title: Persist prompt dismissal/show state and refresh profile after WhatsApp actions
features.description:
Make prompt state durable and keep user state in sync.

Scope
- When the user skips or cancels, persist the prompt as shown/dismissed via backend-supported state.
- When the user successfully enables/connects WhatsApp, refresh the current user/profile state so eligibility updates immediately.
- Ensure no duplicate prompts appear from polling, websocket updates, or refetches.

Acceptance criteria
- Skip/cancel state survives refresh and future sessions.
- Successful connect updates UI state without requiring a manual reload.
- Prompt eligibility is derived from current backend-backed user data, not only local component state.
